summary: K. S. Balasubramanian works in Indology and philosophy. He has served at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Director (attested 2026).

id: P:K. S. J. M. de Vreese
summary: K. S. J. M. de Vreese (1906–1992) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Jean Philippe Vogel (~1932–1936), later serving there as PD of Pāli (1948–1963) and as professor at the University of Amsterdam (1960–1981).
K. Sambasiva Sastri (1879–1946) was an Indology scholar. He succeeded T. Ganapati Sastri (attested 1931) and served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (~1923–1934).

K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who taught Whitney Cox, Hugo David, Steven Edward Lindquist, and Mattia Salvini. He held a professorship at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).

K. V. J. Koshalee specializes in Buddhist studies and archaeology, earning a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a diploma from the Postgraduate Institute of Archaeology. Posts include Senior Lecturer at Kelaniya (2021) and Ruhuna (2025), and Academic Supervisor at PGIBS (attested 2026).

K. V. Puttappa (1904–1994) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, and the University of Mysore (~1927–1929), and he later taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.

K. V. Raman (1934–2024) studied history and archaeology at Madras Christian College under A. J. Boyd, the University of Madras, and the Institute of Archaeology, ASI. He worked for the ASI (~1957–1976) and was Professor and Department Head at Madras (1976–1995).

K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Epigraphical Society of India, Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1981–1987), and Honorary Director at Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).

K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who taught A. N. Krishna Aiyangar and A. N. Srinivasaraghava Aiyangar. He served as Principal of Banaras Hindu University and Central Hindu College (~1935–1940).

K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Supervised by Yongtong Tang, Sentian Wang, and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, he studied at Peking University, the Harvard-Yenching Institute, and Visva-Bharati University (DLitt), where he also taught.

K. de B. Codrington (1899–1986) studied at Corpus Christi College and Wadham College. Specializing in archaeology and Indology, he held posts at the University of Cincinnati (1925–1926), Victoria and Albert Museum (1935–1948), and SOAS as Professor of Indian Archaeology (1948–1966).

Kaetan Andreevich Kossovich (1815–1883) studied under Aleksej Stepanovič Homjakov at Moscow State University. Specializing in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he taught Greek at Tver Gymnasium (1839–1843) and became Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University in 1858.

id: P:Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso
summary: Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Kai Donner (1888–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Otto Donner and at the University of Cambridge (~1911–1912), and later held a post at the University of Helsinki (~1924–1935).

Kaie Mochizuki (b. 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has served at Minobusan University as professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and as university president (attested 2026).
Kaigen Noritake studied Buddhist studies under Kenyu Mitomo and served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) studied under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg (PhD 1900–1907). A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he was principal of Shiba Junior & Senior High School (~1910–1933) and held professorships at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho Universities.

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) studied at Komazawa and Keio Universities. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who lectured at Harvard (~1914–1915), he served at Komazawa University as head teacher (1919), president (1921), and first president (1925–1934).

Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught Takanori Unno and Fujio Taniguchi, and held posts at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and professor (attested 1999–2002).

Kaj Barr (1896–1970) studied Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics under Arthur Christensen, Poul Tuxen, and Friedrich Carl Andreas at Copenhagen and Göttingen. He served as a classical philology lecturer at the University of Copenhagen (1935–1945), succeeding Christensen in 1945.
